verdict.rationale: Only community comments from Ironclad's early launch show it shipped templatized legal documents: users describe 'templatized form entry' and a startup relying on it to handle contractor paperwork, which suggests routine documents without counsel. Current first-party docs mention only company-defined workflow templates and a no-code builder, not a library of vetted standard templates. Community concern about whether the templates were vetted is skepticism, not a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of a pre-built template library, evidence of NDA/agreement/policy coverage, evidence of legal vetting, and current-product corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can start from a library of vetted standard legal templates (NDAs, agreements, policies) instead of hiring counsel for routine documents

citations.quote: Doing intelligent templatized form entry seems really convenient
Whenever we have a new contractor, we shoot them an email (actually now we click a button) and they take care of the rest.
